Instead they are manually created or deleted in a model builder tool. Topological nodes maintained this way are also called "busses".

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the TopologicalNode: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

DCTopologicalIsland.description: An electrically connected subset of the network. DC topological islands can change as the current network state changes, e.g. due to: - disconnect switches or breakers changing state in a SCADA/EMS. - manual creation, change or deletion of topological nodes in a planning tool. Only energised TopologicalNode-s shall be part of the topological island.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DCTopologicalIsland: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

SvInjection.description: The SvInjection reports the calculated bus injection minus the sum of the terminal flows. The terminal flow is positive out from the bus (load sign convention) and bus injection has positive flow into the bus. SvInjection may have the remainder after state estimation or slack after power flow calculation.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvInjection: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

pInjection.name: pInjection
pInjection.description: The active power mismatch between calculated injection and initial injection. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus). Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type ActivePower, in MW.

qInjection.name: qInjection
qInjection.description: The reactive power mismatch between calculated injection and initial injection. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus). CIM type ReactivePower, in MVAr.

SvPowerFlow.description: State variable for power flow. Load convention is used for flow direction. This means flow out from the TopologicalNode into the equipment is positive.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvPowerFlow: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

p.name: p
p.description: The active power flow. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type ActivePower, in MW.

q.name: q
q.description: The reactive power flow. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type ReactivePower, in MVAr.

SvShuntCompensatorSections.description: State variable for the number of sections in service for a shunt compensator.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvShuntCompensatorSections: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

sections.name: sections
sections.description: The number of sections in service as a continuous variable. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero. To get integer value scale with ShuntCompensator.bPerSection. Multiplicity 1..1.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvStatus: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

inService.name: inService
inService.description: The in service status as a result of topology processing. It indicates if the equipment is considered as energized by the power flow. It reflects if the equipment is connected within a solvable island. It does not necessarily reflect whether or not the island was solved by the power flow. Multiplicity 1..1.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvSwitch: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

open.name: open
open.description: The attribute tells if the computed state of the switch is considered open. Multiplicity 1..1.

SvTapStep.description: State variable for transformer tap step.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvTapStep: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

position.name: position
position.description: The floating point tap position. This is not the tap ratio, but rather the tap step position as defined by the related tap changer model and normally is constrained to be within the range of minimum and maximum tap positions. Multiplicity 1..1.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the SvVoltage: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

angle.name: angle
angle.description: The voltage angle of the topological node complex voltage with respect to system reference. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type AngleDegrees, in deg.

v.name: v
v.description: The voltage magnitude at the topological node. The attribute shall be a positive value. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Voltage, in kV.

TopologicalIsland.description: An electrically connected subset of the network. Topological islands can change as the current network state changes, e.g. due to: - disconnect switches or breakers changing state in a SCADA/EMS. - manual creation, change or deletion of topological nodes in a planning tool. Only energised TopologicalNode-s shall be part of the topological island.

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.description: Function block used indicator. true = use of function block is enabled false = use of function block is disabled. Multiplicity 1..1.

RotatingMachineDynamics.description: Abstract parent class for all synchronous and asynchronous machine standard models.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the RotatingMachineDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

damping.name: damping
damping.description: Damping torque coefficient (D) (>= 0). A proportionality constant that, when multiplied by the angular velocity of the rotor poles with respect to the magnetic field (frequency), results in the damping torque. This value is often zero when the sources of damping torques (generator damper windings, load damping effects, etc.) are modelled in detail. Typical value = 0. Multiplicity 1..1.

inertia.name: inertia
inertia.description: Inertia constant of generator or motor and mechanical load (H) (> 0). This is the specification for the stored energy in the rotating mass when operating at rated speed. For a generator, this includes the generator plus all other elements (turbine, exciter) on the same shaft and has units of MW x s. For a motor, it includes the motor plus its mechanical load. Conventional units are PU on the generator MVA base, usually expressed as MW x s / MVA or just s. This value is used in the accelerating power reference frame for operator training simulator solutions. Typical value = 3. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

saturationFactor.name: saturationFactor
saturationFactor.description: Saturation factor at rated terminal voltage (S1) (>= 0). Not used by simplified model. Defined by defined by S(E1) in the SynchronousMachineSaturationParameters diagram. Typical value = 0,02.

saturationFactor120.name: saturationFactor120
saturationFactor120.description: Saturation factor at 120% of rated terminal voltage (S12) (>= RotatingMachineDynamics.saturationFactor). Not used by the simplified model, defined by S(E2) in the SynchronousMachineSaturationParameters diagram. Typical value = 0,12.

statorLeakageReactance.name: statorLeakageReactance
statorLeakageReactance.description: Stator leakage reactance (Xl) (>= 0). Typical value = 0,15. Multiplicity 1..1.

SynchronousMachineSimplified.description: The simplified model represents a synchronous generator as a constant internal voltage behind an impedance (Rs + jXp) as shown in the Simplified diagram. Since internal voltage is held constant, there is no Efd input and any excitation system model will be ignored. There is also no Ifd output. This model should not be used for representing a real generator except, perhaps, small generators whose response is insignificant. The parameters used for the simplified model include: - RotatingMachineDynamics.damping (D); - RotatingMachineDynamics.inertia (H); - RotatingMachineDynamics.statorLeakageReactance (used to exchange jXp for SynchronousMachineSimplified); - RotatingMachineDynamics.statorResistance (Rs).

SynchronousMachineDynamics.description:
Synchronous machine whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model expressed in one of the following forms: - simplified (or classical), where a group of generators or motors is not modelled in detail; - detailed, in equivalent circuit form; - detailed, in time constant reactance form; or - by definition of a user-defined model. It is a common practice to represent small generators by a negative load rather than by a dynamic generator model when performing dynamics simulations. In this case, a SynchronousMachine in the static model is not represented by anything in the dynamics model, instead it is treated as an ordinary load. Parameter details:

SynchronousMachineDetailed.description: All synchronous machine detailed types use a subset of the same data parameters and input/output variables. The several variations differ in the following ways: - the number of equivalent windings that are included; - the way in which saturation is incorporated into the model; - whether or not “subtransient saliency” (X''q not = X''d) is represented. It is not necessary for each simulation tool to have separate models for each of the model types. The same model can often be used for several types by alternative logic within the model. Also, differences in saturation representation might not result in significant model performance differences so model substitutions are often acceptable.

GovCT1.description:
General model for any prime mover with a PID governor, used primarily for combustion turbine and combined cycle units. This model can be used to represent a variety of prime movers controlled by PID governors. It is suitable, for example, for the representation of:
  • gas turbine and single shaft combined cycle turbines
  • diesel engines with modern electronic or digital governors
  • steam turbines where steam is supplied from a large boiler drum or a large header whose pressure is substantially constant over the period under study
  • simple hydro turbines in dam configurations where the water column length is short and water inertia effects are minimal.
Additional information on this model is available in the 2012 IEEE report, Dynamic Models for Turbine-Governors in Power System Studies, 3.1.2.3 pages 3-4 (GGOV1).

dm.name: dm
dm.description: Speed sensitivity coefficient (Dm). Dm can represent either the variation of the engine power with the shaft speed or the variation of maximum power capability with shaft speed. If it is positive it describes the falling slope of the engine speed verses power characteristic as speed increases. A slightly falling characteristic is typical for reciprocating engines and some aero-derivative turbines. If it is negative the engine power is assumed to be unaffected by the shaft speed, but the maximum permissible fuel flow is taken to fall with falling shaft speed. This is characteristic of single-shaft industrial turbines due to exhaust temperature limits. Typical value = 0. Multiplicity 1..1.

dm.name: dm
dm.description: Speed sensitivity coefficient (Dm). Dm can represent either the variation of the engine power with the shaft speed or the variation of maximum power capability with shaft speed. If it is positive it describes the falling slope of the engine speed verses power characteristic as speed increases. A slightly falling characteristic is typical for reciprocating engines and some aero-derivative turbines. If it is negative the engine power is assumed to be unaffected by the shaft speed, but the maximum permissible fuel flow is taken to fall with falling shaft speed. This is characteristic of single-shaft industrial turbines due to exhaust temperature limits. Typical value = 0. Multiplicity 1..1.

ExcIEEEAC3A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type AC3A model. The model represents the field-controlled alternator-rectifier excitation systems designated type AC3A. These excitation systems include an alternator main exciter with non-controlled rectifiers. The exciter employs self-excitation, and the voltage regulator power is derived from the exciter output voltage. Therefore, this system has an additional nonlinearity, simulated by the use of a multiplier whose inputs are the voltage regulator command signal, Va, and the exciter output voltage, Efd, times KR. This model is applicable to excitation systems employing static voltage regulators. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 6.3.

ExcIEEEAC4A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type AC4A model. The model represents type AC4A alternator-supplied controlled-rectifier excitation system which is quite different from the other types of AC systems. This high initial response excitation system utilizes a full thyristor bridge in the exciter output circuit. The voltage regulator controls the firing of the thyristor bridges. The exciter alternator uses an independent voltage regulator to control its output voltage to a constant value. These effects are not modelled; however, transient loading effects on the exciter alternator are included. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 6.4.

ExcIEEEAC5A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type AC5A model. The model represents a simplified model for brushless excitation systems. The regulator is supplied from a source, such as a permanent magnet generator, which is not affected by system disturbances. Unlike other AC models, this model uses loaded rather than open circuit exciter saturation data in the same way as it is used for the DC models. Because the model has been widely implemented by the industry, it is sometimes used to represent other types of systems when either detailed data for them are not available or simplified models are required. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 6.5.

ExcIEEEAC7B.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type AC7B model. The model represents excitation systems which consist of an AC alternator with either stationary or rotating rectifiers to produce the DC field requirements. It is an upgrade to earlier AC excitation systems, which replace only the controls but retain the AC alternator and diode rectifier bridge. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 6.7. Note, however, that in IEEE 421.5-2005, the [1 / sTE] block is shown as [1 / (1 + sTE)], which is incorrect.

The representation of the brushless exciter (TE, KE, SE, KC, KD) is similar to the model type AC2A. The type AC8B model can be used to represent static voltage regulators applied to brushless excitation systems. ExcIEEEDC2A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type DC2A model. This model represents field-controlled DC commutator exciters with continuously acting voltage regulators having supplies obtained from the generator or auxiliary bus. It differs from the type DC1A model only in the voltage regulator output limits, which are now proportional to terminal voltage VT. It is representative of solid-state replacements for various forms of older mechanical and rotating amplifier regulating equipment connected to DC commutator exciters. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 5.2.

ExcIEEEDC3A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type DC3A model. This model represents older systems, in particular those DC commutator exciters with non-continuously acting regulators that were commonly used before the development of the continuously acting varieties. These systems respond at basically two different rates, depending upon the magnitude of voltage error. For small errors, adjustment is made periodically with a signal to a motor-operated rheostat. Larger errors cause resistors to be quickly shorted or inserted and a strong forcing signal applied to the exciter. Continuous motion of the motor-operated rheostat occurs for these larger error signals, even though it is bypassed by contactor action. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 5.3.

ExcIEEEST1A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST1A model. ExcIEEEST3A.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST3A model. Some static systems utilize a field voltage control loop to linearize the exciter control characteristic. This also makes the output independent of supply source variations until supply limitations are reached. These systems utilize a variety of controlled-rectifier designs: full thyristor complements or hybrid bridges in either series or shunt configurations. The power source can consist of only a potential source, either fed from the machine terminals or from internal windings. Some designs can have compound power sources utilizing both machine potential and current. These power sources are represented as phasor combinations of machine terminal current and voltage and are accommodated by suitable parameters in model type ST3A which is represented by ExcIEEEST3A. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 7.3.

ExcIEEEST4B.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST4B model. This model is a variation of the type ST3A model, with a proportional plus integral (PI) regulator block replacing the lag-lead regulator characteristic that is in the ST3A model. Both potential and compound source rectifier excitation systems are modelled. The PI regulator blocks have non-windup limits that are represented. The voltage regulator of this model is typically implemented digitally. Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 7.4.

ExcIEEEST5B.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST5B model. The type ST5B excitation system is a variation of the type ST1A model, with alternative overexcitation and underexcitation inputs and additional limits. ExcIEEEST7B.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST7B model. This model is representative of static potential-source excitation systems. In this system, the AVR consists of a PI voltage regulator. A phase lead-lag filter in series allows the introduction of a derivative function, typically used with brushless excitation systems. In that case, the regulator is of the PID type. In addition, the terminal voltage channel includes a phase lead-lag filter. The AVR includes the appropriate inputs on its reference for overexcitation limiter (OEL1), underexcitation limiter (UEL), stator current limiter (SCL), and current compensator (DROOP). All these limitations, when they work at voltage reference level, keep the PSS (VS signal from PSS) in operation. However, the UEL limitation can also be transferred to the high value (HV) gate acting on the output signal. In addition, the output signal passes through a low value (LV) gate for a ceiling overexcitation limiter (OEL2). Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 7.7.

OverexcLimIEEE.description: The over excitation limiter model is intended to represent the significant features of OELs necessary for some large-scale system studies. It is the result of a pragmatic approach to obtain a model that can be widely applied with attainable data from generator owners. An attempt to include all variations in the functionality of OELs and duplicate how they interact with the rest of the excitation systems would likely result in a level of application insufficient for the studies for which they are intended. Reference: IEEE OEL 421.5-2005, 9.

PssIEEE4B.description: IEEE 421.5-2005 type PSS4B power system stabilizer. The PSS4B model represents a structure based on multiple working frequency bands. Three separate bands, respectively dedicated to the low-, intermediate- and high-frequency modes of oscillations, are used in this delta omega (speed input) PSS. There is an error in the in IEEE 421.5-2005 PSS4B model: the Pe input should read –Pe. This implies that the input Pe needs to be multiplied by -1. Reference: IEEE 4B 421.5-2005, 8.4. Parameter details: This model has 2 input signals. They have the following fixed types (expressed in terms of InputSignalKind values): the first one is of rotorAngleFrequencyDeviation type and the second one is of generatorElectricalPower type.

VCompIEEEType1.description:
Terminal voltage transducer and load compensator as defined in IEEE 421.5-2005, 4. This model is common to all excitation system models described in the IEEE Standard. Parameter details:
  1. If Rc and Xc are set to zero, the load compensation is not employed and the behaviour is as a simple sensing circuit.
  1. If all parameters (Rc, Xc and Tr) are set to zero, the standard model VCompIEEEType1 is bypassed.
Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005 4.

VCompIEEEType2.description:
Terminal voltage transducer and load compensator as defined in IEEE 421.5-2005, 4. This model is designed to cover the following types of compensation:
  • reactive droop;
  • transformer-drop or line-drop compensation;
  • reactive differential compensation known also as cross-current compensation.
Reference: IEEE 421.5-2005, 4..

pfrac.description: Fraction of constant-power load to be represented by this motor model (PFRAC) (>= 0,0 and <= 1,0). Typical value = 0,5. Multiplicity 1..1.

LoadGenericNonLinear.description: Generic non-linear dynamic (GNLD) load. This model can be used in mid-term and long-term voltage stability simulations (i.e., to study voltage collapse), as it can replace a more detailed representation of aggregate load, including induction motors, thermostatically controlled and static loads.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the LoadGenericNonLinear: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

bs.name: bs
bs.description: Steady state voltage index for reactive power (BS). Multiplicity 1..1.

bt.name: bt
bt.description: Transient voltage index for reactive power (BT). Multiplicity 1..1.

genericNonLinearLoadModelType.name: genericNonLinearLoadModelType
genericNonLinearLoadModelType.description: Type of generic non-linear load model. Multiplicity 1..1.

ls.name: ls
ls.description: Steady state voltage index for active power (LS). Multiplicity 1..1.

lt.name: lt
lt.description: Transient voltage index for active power (LT). Multiplicity 1..1.

tp.name: tp
tp.description: Time constant of lag function of active power (TP) (> 0). Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

tq.name: tq
tq.description: Time constant of lag function of reactive power (TQ) (> 0). Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

LoadDynamics.description: Load whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font> A standard feature of dynamic load behaviour modelling is the ability to associate the same behaviour to multiple energy consumers by means of a single load definition. The load model is always applied to individual bus loads (energy consumers).

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the LoadDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

LoadAggregate.description: Aggregate loads are used to represent all or part of the real and reactive load from one or more loads in the static (power flow) data. This load is usually the aggregation of many individual load devices and the load model is an approximate representation of the aggregate response of the load devices to system disturbances. Standard aggregate load model comprised of static and/or dynamic components. A static load model represents the sensitivity of the real and reactive power consumed by the load to the amplitude and frequency of the bus voltage. A dynamic load model can be used to represent the aggregate response of the motor components of the load.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the LoadAggregate: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

LoadStatic.description: General static load. This model represents the sensitivity of the real and reactive power consumed by the load to the amplitude and frequency of the bus voltage.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the LoadStatic: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

ep1.name: ep1
ep1.description: First term voltage exponent for active power (Ep1). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

ep2.name: ep2
ep2.description: Second term voltage exponent for active power (Ep2). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

ep3.name: ep3
ep3.description: Third term voltage exponent for active power (Ep3). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

eq1.name: eq1
eq1.description: First term voltage exponent for reactive power (Eq1). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

eq2.name: eq2
eq2.description: Second term voltage exponent for reactive power (Eq2). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

eq3.name: eq3
eq3.description: Third term voltage exponent for reactive power (Eq3). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = exponential.

kp1.name: kp1
kp1.description: First term voltage coefficient for active power (Kp1). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kp2.name: kp2
kp2.description: Second term voltage coefficient for active power (Kp2). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kp3.name: kp3
kp3.description: Third term voltage coefficient for active power (Kp3). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kp4.name: kp4
kp4.description: Frequency coefficient for active power (Kp4) (not = 0 if .staticLoadModelType = zIP2). Used only when .staticLoadModelType = zIP2.

kpf.name: kpf
kpf.description: Frequency deviation coefficient for active power (Kpf). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kq1.name: kq1
kq1.description: First term voltage coefficient for reactive power (Kq1). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kq2.name: kq2
kq2.description: Second term voltage coefficient for reactive power (Kq2). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kq3.name: kq3
kq3.description: Third term voltage coefficient for reactive power (Kq3). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

kq4.name: kq4
kq4.description: Frequency coefficient for reactive power (Kq4) (not = 0 when .staticLoadModelType = zIP2). Used only when .staticLoadModelType - zIP2.

kqf.name: kqf
kqf.description: Frequency deviation coefficient for reactive power (Kqf). Not used when .staticLoadModelType = constantZ.

staticLoadModelType.name: staticLoadModelType
staticLoadModelType.description: Type of static load model. Typical value = constantZ. Multiplicity 1..1.

LoadMotor.description: Aggregate induction motor load. This model is used to represent a fraction of an ordinary load as "induction motor load". It allows a load that is treated as an ordinary constant power in power flow analysis to be represented by an induction motor in dynamic simulation. This model is intended for representation of aggregations of many motors dispersed through a load represented at a high voltage bus but where there is no information on the characteristics of individual motors. Either a "one-cage" or "two-cage" model of the induction machine can be modelled. Magnetic saturation is not modelled. This model treats a fraction of the constant power part of a load as a motor. During initialisation, the initial power drawn by the motor is set equal to Pfrac times the constant P part of the static load. The remainder of the load is left as a static load. The reactive power demand of the motor is calculated during initialisation as a function of voltage at the load bus. This reactive power demand can…

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the LoadMotor: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

d.name: d
d.description: Damping factor (D). Unit = delta P/delta speed. Typical value = 2. Multiplicity 1..1.

h.name: h
h.description: Inertia constant (H) (>= 0). Typical value = 0,4. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

lfac.name: lfac
lfac.description: Loading factor (Lfac). The ratio of initial P to motor MVA base. Typical value = 0,8. Multiplicity 1..1.

pfrac.name: pfrac
pfrac.description: Fraction of constant-power load to be represented by this motor model (Pfrac) (>= 0,0 and <= 1,0). Typical value = 0,3. Multiplicity 1..1.

tbkr.name: tbkr
tbkr.description: Circuit breaker operating time (Tbkr) (>= 0). Typical value = 0,08. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

tpo.name: tpo
tpo.description: Transient rotor time constant (Tpo) (>= 0). Typical value = 1. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

tppo.name: tppo
tppo.description: Subtransient rotor time constant (Tppo) (>= 0). Typical value = 0,02. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

tv.name: tv
tv.description: Voltage trip pickup time (Tv) (>= 0). Typical value = 0,1. Multiplicity 1..1. CIM type Seconds, in s.

vt.name: vt
vt.description: Voltage threshold for tripping (Vt). Typical value = 0,7. Multiplicity 1..1.

CSCDynamics.description: CSC function block whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font>.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the CSCDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

HVDCDynamics.description: HVDC whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font>.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the HVDCDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

VSCDynamics.description: VSC function block whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font>.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the VSCDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

StaticVarCompensatorDynamics.description: Static var compensator whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font>.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the StaticVarCompensatorDynamics: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

Diagram.description: The diagram being exchanged. The coordinate system is a standard Cartesian coordinate system and the orientation attribute defines the orientation. The initial view related attributes can be used to specify an initial view with the x,y coordinates of the diagonal points.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the Diagram: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

orientation.name: orientation
orientation.description: Coordinate system orientation of the diagram. A positive orientation gives standard “right-hand” orientation, with negative orientation indicating a “left-hand” orientation. For 2D diagrams, a positive orientation will result in X values increasing from left to right and Y values increasing from bottom to top. A negative orientation gives the “left-hand” orientation (favoured by computer graphics displays) with X values increasing from left to right and Y values increasing from top to bottom. Multiplicity 1..1.

x1InitialView.name: x1InitialView
x1InitialView.description: X coordinate of the first corner of the initial view.

x2InitialView.name: x2InitialView
x2InitialView.description: X coordinate of the second corner of the initial view.

y1InitialView.name: y1InitialView
y1InitialView.description: Y coordinate of the first corner of the initial view.

y2InitialView.name: y2InitialView
y2InitialView.description: Y coordinate of the second corner of the initial view.

DiagramObject.description: An object that defines one or more points in a given space. This object can be associated with anything that specializes IdentifiedObject. For single line diagrams such objects typically include such items as analog values, breakers, disconnectors, power transformers, and transmission lines.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DiagramObject: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

drawingOrder.name: drawingOrder
drawingOrder.description: The drawing order of this element. The higher the number, the later the element is drawn in sequence. This is used to ensure that elements that overlap are rendered in the correct order.

isPolygon.name: isPolygon
isPolygon.description: Defines whether or not the diagram objects points define the boundaries of a polygon or the routing of a polyline. If this value is true then a receiving application should consider the first and last points to be connected.

offsetX.name: offsetX
offsetX.description: The offset in the X direction. This is used for defining the offset from centre for rendering an icon (the default is that a single point specifies the centre of the icon). The offset is in per-unit with 0 indicating there is no offset from the horizontal centre of the icon. -0.5 indicates it is offset by 50% to the left and 0.5 indicates an offset of 50% to the right.

offsetY.name: offsetY
offsetY.description: The offset in the Y direction. This is used for defining the offset from centre for rendering an icon (the default is that a single point specifies the centre of the icon). The offset is in per-unit with 0 indicating there is no offset from the vertical centre of the icon. The offset direction is dependent on the orientation of the diagram, with -0.5 and 0.5 indicating an offset of +/- 50% on the vertical axis.

rotation.name: rotation
rotation.description: Sets the angle of rotation of the diagram object. Zero degrees is pointing to the top of the diagram. Rotation is clockwise. DiagramObject.rotation=0 has the following meaning: The connection point of an element which has one terminal is pointing to the top side of the diagram. The connection point "From side" of an element which has more than one terminal is pointing to the top side of the diagram. DiagramObject.rotation=90 has the following meaning: The connection point of an element which has one terminal is pointing to the right hand side of the diagram. The connection point "From side" of an element which has more than one terminal is pointing to the right hand side of the diagram. CIM type AngleDegrees, in deg.

DiagramObjectGluePoint.description: This is used for grouping diagram object points from different diagram objects that are considered to be glued together in a diagram even if they are not at the exact same coordinates.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DiagramObjectGluePoint: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

DiagramObjectPoint.description: A point in a given space defined by 3 coordinates and associated to a diagram object. The coordinates may be positive or negative as the origin does not have to be in the corner of a diagram.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DiagramObjectPoint: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

sequenceNumber.name: sequenceNumber
sequenceNumber.description: The sequence position of the point, used for defining the order of points for diagram objects acting as a polyline or polygon with more than one point. The attribute shall be a positive value.

xPosition.name: xPosition
xPosition.description: The X coordinate of this point. Multiplicity 1..1.

yPosition.name: yPosition
yPosition.description: The Y coordinate of this point. Multiplicity 1..1.

zPosition.name: zPosition
zPosition.description: The Z coordinate of this point.

DiagramObjectStyle.description: A reference to a style used by the originating system for a diagram object. A diagram object style describes information such as line thickness, shape such as circle or rectangle etc, and colour.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DiagramObjectStyle: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

DiagramStyle.description: The diagram style refers to a style used by the originating system for a diagram. A diagram style describes information such as schematic, geographic, etc.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the DiagramStyle: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

TextDiagramObject.description: A diagram object for placing free-text or text derived from an associated domain object.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the TextDiagramObject: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

text.name: text
text.description: The text that is displayed by this text diagram object. Multiplicity 1..1.

VisibilityLayer.description: Layers are typically used for grouping diagram objects according to themes and scales. Themes are used to display or hide certain information (e.g., lakes, borders), while scales are used for hiding or displaying information depending on the current zoom level (hide text when it is too small to be read, or when it exceeds the screen size). This is also called de-cluttering. CIM based graphics exchange supports an m:n relationship between diagram objects and layers. The importing system shall convert an m:n case into an appropriate 1:n representation if the importing system does not support m:n.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the VisibilityLayer: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

drawingOrder.name: drawingOrder
drawingOrder.description: The drawing order for this layer. The higher the number, the later the layer and the objects within it are rendered.

ServiceLocation.description: A real estate location, commonly referred to as premises.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the ServiceLocation: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

WorkLocation.description: Information about a particular location for various forms of work.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the WorkLocation: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the CoordinateSystem: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

crsUrn.name: crsUrn
crsUrn.description: A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for the coordinate reference system (crs) used to define 'Location.PositionPoints'. An example would be the European Petroleum Survey Group (EPSG) code for a coordinate reference system, defined in URN under the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) namespace as: urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::XXXX, where XXXX is an EPSG code (a full list of codes can be found at the EPSG Registry web site http://www.epsg-registry.org/). To define the coordinate system as being WGS84 (latitude, longitude) using an EPSG OGC, this attribute would be urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4236. A profile should limit this code to a set of allowed URNs agreed to by all sending and receiving parties. Multiplicity 1..1.

Location.description: The place, scene, or point of something where someone or something has been, is, and/or will be at a given moment in time. It can be defined with one or more position points (coordinates) in a given coordinate system.

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the Location: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

PositionPoint.description: Set of spatial coordinates that determine a point, defined in the coordinate system specified in 'Location.CoordinateSystem'. Use a single position point instance to describe a point-oriented location. Use a sequence of position points to describe a line-oriented object (physical location of non-point oriented objects like cables or lines), or area of an object (like a substation or a geographical zone - in this case, have first and last position point with the same values).

rdfId.name: rdfId
rdfId.description: The identifier of the PositionPoint: the rdf:ID of its element in a CGMES (CIMXML) file, or the rdf:about, without its leading #, of the elements that describe it in other profiles. For an IdentifiedObject it is derived from its mRID.

sequenceNumber.name: sequenceNumber
sequenceNumber.description: Zero-relative sequence number of this point within a series of points.

ACDCConverter_HAS_PCC_TERMINAL_Terminal.description: Point of common coupling terminal for this converter DC side. It is typically the terminal on the power transformer (or switch) closest to the AC network. Each ACDCConverter has at most one Terminal. The inverse role is Terminal.ConverterDCSides: each Terminal has zero or more ACDCConverter.

ACDCConverterDCTerminal_HAS_DC_CONDUCTIN.description: A DC converter terminal belong to an DC converter. Each ACDCConverterDCTerminal has exactly one ACDCConverter. The inverse role is ACDCConverter.DCTerminals: each ACDCConverter has zero or more ACDCConverterDCTerminal.

ACDCTerminal_HAS_BUS_NAME_MARKER_BusName.description: The bus name marker used to name the bus (topological node). Each ACDCTerminal has at most one BusNameMarker. The inverse role is BusNameMarker.Terminal: each BusNameMarker has one or more ACDCTerminal.

AccumulatorLimit_HAS_LIMIT_SET_Accumulat.description: The set of limits. Each AccumulatorLimit has exactly one AccumulatorLimitSet. The inverse role is AccumulatorLimitSet.Limits: each AccumulatorLimitSet has one or more AccumulatorLimit.

AccumulatorLimitSet_HAS_MEASUREMENTS_Acc.description: The Measurements using the LimitSet. Each AccumulatorLimitSet has one or more Accumulator. The inverse role is Accumulator.LimitSets: each Accumulator has zero or more AccumulatorLimitSet.

AccumulatorReset_HAS_ACCUMULATOR_VALUE_A.description: The accumulator value that is reset by the command. Each AccumulatorReset has exactly one AccumulatorValue. The inverse role is AccumulatorValue.AccumulatorReset: each AccumulatorValue has at most one AccumulatorReset.

AccumulatorValue_HAS_ACCUMULATOR_Accumul.description: Measurement to which this value is connected. Each AccumulatorValue has exactly one Accumulator. The inverse role is Accumulator.AccumulatorValues: each Accumulator has zero or more AccumulatorValue.

AnalogControl_HAS_ANALOG_VALUE_AnalogVal.description: The MeasurementValue that is controlled. Each AnalogControl has exactly one AnalogValue. The inverse role is AnalogValue.AnalogControl: each AnalogValue has at most one AnalogControl.

AnalogLimit_HAS_LIMIT_SET_AnalogLimitSet.description: The set of limits. Each AnalogLimit has exactly one AnalogLimitSet. The inverse role is AnalogLimitSet.Limits: each AnalogLimitSet has zero or more AnalogLimit.

AnalogLimitSet_HAS_MEASUREMENTS_Analog.description: The Measurements using the LimitSet. Each AnalogLimitSet has one or more Analog. The inverse role is Analog.LimitSets: each Analog has zero or more AnalogLimitSet.

AnalogValue_HAS_ANALOG_Analog.description: Measurement to which this value is connected. Each AnalogValue has exactly one Analog. The inverse role is Analog.AnalogValues: each Analog has zero or more AnalogValue.

AsynchronousMachineDynamics_HAS_ASYNCHRO.description: Asynchronous machine to which this asynchronous machine dynamics model applies. Each AsynchronousMachineDynamics has exactly one AsynchronousMachine. The inverse role is AsynchronousMachine.AsynchronousMachineDynamics: each AsynchronousMachine has at most one AsynchronousMachineDynamics.

AuxiliaryEquipment_HAS_TERMINAL_Terminal.description: The Terminal at the equipment where the AuxiliaryEquipment is attached. Each AuxiliaryEquipment has exactly one Terminal. The inverse role is Terminal.AuxiliaryEquipment: each Terminal has zero or more AuxiliaryEquipment.

Bay_HAS_VOLTAGE_LEVEL_VoltageLevel.description: The voltage level containing this bay. Each Bay has exactly one VoltageLevel. The inverse role is VoltageLevel.Bays: each VoltageLevel has zero or more Bay.

BusNameMarker_HAS_REPORTING_GROUP_Report.description: The reporting group to which this bus name marker belongs. Each BusNameMarker has at most one ReportingGroup. The inverse role is ReportingGroup.BusNameMarker: each ReportingGroup has zero or more BusNameMarker.

CSCDynamics_HAS_CS_CONVERTER_CsConverter.description: Current source converter to which current source converter dynamics model applies. Each CSCDynamics has exactly one CsConverter. The inverse role is CsConverter.CSCDynamics: each CsConverter has at most one CSCDynamics.

Clamp_HAS_AC_LINE_SEGMENT_ACLineSegment.description: The line segment to which the clamp is connected. Each Clamp has exactly one ACLineSegment. The inverse role is ACLineSegment.Clamp: each ACLineSegment has zero or more Clamp.

Command_HAS_DISCRETE_VALUE_DiscreteValue.description: The MeasurementValue that is controlled. Each Command has exactly one DiscreteValue. The inverse role is DiscreteValue.Command: each DiscreteValue has at most one Command.

Command_HAS_VALUE_ALIAS_SET_ValueAliasSe.description: The ValueAliasSet used for translation of a Control value to a name. Each Command has at most one ValueAliasSet. The inverse role is ValueAliasSet.Commands: each ValueAliasSet has zero or more Command.

ConductingEquipment_HAS_BASE_VOLTAGE_Bas.description: Base voltage of this conducting equipment. Use only when there is no voltage level container used and only one base voltage applies. For example, not used for transformers. Each ConductingEquipment has at most one BaseVoltage. The inverse role is BaseVoltage.ConductingEquipment: each BaseVoltage has zero or more ConductingEquipment.

ConformLoad_HAS_LOAD_GROUP_ConformLoadGr.description: Group of this ConformLoad. Each ConformLoad has exactly one ConformLoadGroup. The inverse role is ConformLoadGroup.EnergyConsumers: each ConformLoadGroup has one or more ConformLoad.

ConformLoadSchedule_HAS_CONFORM_LOAD_GRO.description: The ConformLoadGroup where the ConformLoadSchedule belongs. Each ConformLoadSchedule has exactly one ConformLoadGroup. The inverse role is ConformLoadGroup.ConformLoadSchedules: each ConformLoadGroup has zero or more ConformLoadSchedule.

ConnectivityNode_HAS_CONNECTIVITY_NODE_C.description: Container of this connectivity node. Each ConnectivityNode has exactly one ConnectivityNodeContainer. The inverse role is ConnectivityNodeContainer.ConnectivityNodes: each ConnectivityNodeContainer has zero or more ConnectivityNode.

ConnectivityNode_HAS_TOPOLOGICAL_NODE_To.description: The topological node to which this connectivity node is assigned. May depend on the current state of switches in the network. Each ConnectivityNode has exactly one TopologicalNode. The inverse role is TopologicalNode.ConnectivityNodes: each TopologicalNode has zero or more ConnectivityNode.

Control_HAS_POWER_SYSTEM_RESOURCE_PowerS.description: Regulating device governed by this control output. Each Control has at most one PowerSystemResource. The inverse role is PowerSystemResource.Controls: each PowerSystemResource has zero or more Control.

ControlArea_HAS_ENERGY_AREA_EnergyArea.description: The energy area that is forecast from this control area specification. Each ControlArea has exactly one EnergyArea. The inverse role is EnergyArea.ControlArea: each EnergyArea has at most one ControlArea.

ControlAreaGeneratingUnit_HAS_CONTROL_AR.description: The parent control area for the generating unit specifications. Each ControlAreaGeneratingUnit has exactly one ControlArea. The inverse role is ControlArea.ControlAreaGeneratingUnit: each ControlArea has zero or more ControlAreaGeneratingUnit.

ControlAreaGeneratingUnit_HAS_GENERATING.description: The generating unit specified for this control area. Note that a control area should include a GeneratingUnit only once. Each ControlAreaGeneratingUnit has exactly one GeneratingUnit. The inverse role is GeneratingUnit.ControlAreaGeneratingUnit: each GeneratingUnit has zero or more ControlAreaGeneratingUnit.

CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics_HAS.description: High-pressure synchronous machine with which this cross-compound turbine governor is associated. Each CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics has exactly one SynchronousMachineDynamics. The inverse role is SynchronousMachineDynamics.CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDyanmics: each SynchronousMachineDynamics has at most one CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics.

Low-pressure synchronous machine with which this cross-compound turbine governor is associated. Each CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics has exactly one SynchronousMachineDynamics. The inverse role is SynchronousMachineDynamics.CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics: each SynchronousMachineDynamics has at most one CrossCompoundTurbineGovernorDynamics.

CurveData_HAS_CURVE_Curve.description: The curve of this curve data point. Each CurveData has exactly one Curve. The inverse role is Curve.CurveDatas: each Curve has one or more CurveData.

Cut_HAS_AC_LINE_SEGMENT_ACLineSegment.description: The line segment to which the cut is applied. Each Cut has exactly one ACLineSegment. The inverse role is ACLineSegment.Cut: each ACLineSegment has zero or more Cut.

DCBaseTerminal_HAS_DC_NODE_DCNode.description: The DC connectivity node to which this DC base terminal connects with zero impedance. Each DCBaseTerminal has at most one DCNode. The inverse role is DCNode.DCTerminals: each DCNode has zero or more DCBaseTerminal.

DCNode_HAS_DC_EQUIPMENT_CONTAINER_DCEqui.description: The DC container for the DC nodes. Each DCNode has exactly one DCEquipmentContainer. The inverse role is DCEquipmentContainer.DCNodes: each DCEquipmentContainer has zero or more DCNode.

DiagramObject_HAS_DIAGRAM_OBJECT_STYLE_D.description: A diagram object has a style associated that provides a reference for the style used in the originating system. Each DiagramObject has at most one DiagramObjectStyle. The inverse role is DiagramObjectStyle.StyledObjects: each DiagramObjectStyle has zero or more DiagramObject.

DiagramObject_HAS_IDENTIFIED_OBJECT_Iden.description: The domain object to which this diagram object is associated. Each DiagramObject has at most one IdentifiedObject. The inverse role is IdentifiedObject.DiagramObjects: each IdentifiedObject has zero or more DiagramObject.

DiagramObjectPoint_HAS_DIAGRAM_OBJECT_Di.description: The diagram object with which the points are associated. Each DiagramObjectPoint has exactly one DiagramObject. The inverse role is DiagramObject.DiagramObjectPoints: each DiagramObject has zero or more DiagramObjectPoint.

DiagramObjectPoint_HAS_DIAGRAM_OBJECT_GL.description: The 'glue' point to which this point is associated. Each DiagramObjectPoint has at most one DiagramObjectGluePoint. DiscontinuousExcitationControlDynamics_H.description: Excitation system model with which this discontinuous excitation control model is associated. DiscreteValue_HAS_DISCRETE_Discrete.description: Measurement to which this value is connected. Each DiscreteValue has exactly one Discrete. The inverse role is Discrete.DiscreteValues: each Discrete has zero or more DiscreteValue.

EnergyConsumer_HAS_LOAD_DYNAMICS_LoadDyn.description: Load dynamics model used to describe dynamic behaviour of this energy consumer. Each EnergyConsumer has at most one LoadDynamics. The inverse role is LoadDynamics.EnergyConsumer: each LoadDynamics has zero or more EnergyConsumer.

EnergyConsumer_HAS_LOAD_RESPONSE_LoadRes.description: The load response characteristic of this load. If missing, this load is assumed to be constant power. EnergySource_HAS_ENERGY_SCHEDULING_TYPE_.description: Energy Scheduling Type of an Energy Source. Each EnergySource has at most one EnergySchedulingType. The inverse role is EnergySchedulingType.EnergySource: each EnergySchedulingType has zero or more EnergySource.

Equipment_HAS_EQUIPMENT_CONTAINER_Equipm.description: Container of this equipment. Each Equipment has at most one EquipmentContainer. The inverse role is EquipmentContainer.Equipments: each EquipmentContainer has zero or more Equipment.

EquivalentEquipment_HAS_EQUIVALENT_NETWO.description: The equivalent where the reduced model belongs. Each EquivalentEquipment has at most one EquivalentNetwork. The inverse role is EquivalentNetwork.EquivalentEquipments: each EquivalentNetwork has zero or more EquivalentEquipment.

EquivalentInjection_HAS_REACTIVE_CAPABIL.description: The reactive capability curve used by this equivalent injection. Each EquivalentInjection has at most one ReactiveCapabilityCurve. The inverse role is ReactiveCapabilityCurve.EquivalentInjection: each ReactiveCapabilityCurve has zero or more EquivalentInjection.

ExcitationSystemDynamics_HAS_SYNCHRONOUS.description: Synchronous machine model with which this excitation system model is associated. FossilFuel_HAS_THERMAL_GENERATING_UNIT_T.description: A thermal generating unit may have one or more fossil fuels. Each FossilFuel has exactly one ThermalGeneratingUnit. The inverse role is ThermalGeneratingUnit.FossilFuels: each ThermalGeneratingUnit has zero or more FossilFuel.

GenICompensationForGenJ_HAS_SYNCHRONOUS_.description: Standard synchronous machine out of which current flow is being compensated for. The inverse role is VCompIEEEType2.GenICompensationForGenJ: each VCompIEEEType2 has between 2 and * GenICompensationForGenJ.

GrossToNetActivePowerCurve_HAS_GENERATIN.description: A generating unit may have a gross active power to net active power curve, describing the losses and auxiliary power requirements of the unit. HydroGeneratingUnit_HAS_HYDRO_POWER_PLAN.description: The hydro generating unit belongs to a hydro power plant. Each HydroGeneratingUnit has at most one HydroPowerPlant. The inverse role is HydroPowerPlant.HydroGeneratingUnits: each HydroPowerPlant has zero or more HydroGeneratingUnit.

HydroPump_HAS_HYDRO_POWER_PLANT_HydroPow.description: The hydro pump may be a member of a pumped storage plant or a pump for distributing water. Each HydroPump has at most one HydroPowerPlant. The inverse role is HydroPowerPlant.HydroPumps: each HydroPowerPlant has zero or more HydroPump.

HydroPump_HAS_ROTATING_MACHINE_RotatingM.description: The synchronous machine drives the turbine which moves the water from a low elevation to a higher elevation. The inverse role is RotatingMachine.HydroPump: each RotatingMachine has at most one HydroPump.

Line_HAS_REGION_SubGeographicalRegion.description: The sub-geographical region of the line. Each Line has at most one SubGeographicalRegion. The inverse role is SubGeographicalRegion.Lines: each SubGeographicalRegion has zero or more Line.

LoadGroup_HAS_SUB_LOAD_AREA_SubLoadArea.description: The SubLoadArea where the Loadgroup belongs. Each LoadGroup has exactly one SubLoadArea. The inverse role is SubLoadArea.LoadGroups: each SubLoadArea has one or more LoadGroup.

LoadStatic_HAS_LOAD_AGGREGATE_LoadAggreg.description: Aggregate load to which this aggregate static load belongs. Each LoadStatic has exactly one LoadAggregate. The inverse role is LoadAggregate.LoadStatic: each LoadAggregate has at most one LoadStatic.

Each MeasurementValue has exactly one MeasurementValueSource. The inverse role is MeasurementValueSource.MeasurementValues: each MeasurementValueSource has zero or more MeasurementValue.

MeasurementValueQuality_HAS_MEASUREMENT_.description: A MeasurementValue has a MeasurementValueQuality associated with it. Each MeasurementValueQuality has exactly one MeasurementValue. The inverse role is MeasurementValue.MeasurementValueQuality: each MeasurementValue has at most one MeasurementValueQuality.

The inverse role is AsynchronousMachineDynamics.MechanicalLoadDynamics: each AsynchronousMachineDynamics has at most one MechanicalLoadDynamics.

MechanicalLoadDynamics_HAS_SYNCHRONOUS_M.description: Synchronous machine model with which this mechanical load model is associated. MechanicalLoadDynamics shall have either an association to SynchronousMachineDynamics or AsynchronousMachineDyanmics. Each MechanicalLoadDynamics has at most one SynchronousMachineDynamics. The inverse role is SynchronousMachineDynamics.MechanicalLoadDynamics: each SynchronousMachineDynamics has at most one MechanicalLoadDynamics.

MutualCoupling_HAS_FIRST_TERMINAL_Termin.description: The starting terminal for the calculation of distances along the first branch of the mutual coupling. Normally MutualCoupling would only be used for terminals of AC line segments. The first and second terminals of a mutual coupling should point to different AC line segments. Each MutualCoupling has exactly one Terminal. The inverse role is Terminal.HasFirstMutualCoupling: each Terminal has zero or more MutualCoupling.

MutualCoupling_HAS_SECOND_TERMINAL_Termi.description: The starting terminal for the calculation of distances along the second branch of the mutual coupling.
